Look at what actually generated the arms — p4, p5 and p7 all flip Bullish mechanically on any violent up-day (vol expansion on upside, volume z on an up day, OI building with price), so a single impulsive session manufactures three "new" Bullish labels across the entire watchlist at once. The second checkpoint is the only thing distinguishing a real setup from a one-day squeeze, and this book has already paid for skipping that lesson — four staged-entry halves (CAKE/ETH/ZEC/MORPHO) were cut yesterday for exactly this failure mode. **The counter-case that does concern me** is the other direction: three simultaneous arms into an F&G that has sprinted +33 points means tomorrow's AM could hand me multiple confirmed candidates at once, at the top of the move, with sector caps and Section 8 floors as the only brakes. The rubric's Bullish branch is genuinely narrow. Flagged for the monthly review as a possible p1 asymmetry: if p1 can only realistically print Bearish or Neutral in a rising tape, it is a one-directional parameter and should not be counted as a full tenth of the gate.

Pre-mortem (PM): **Scenario — BTC −15% overnight.** With zero positions the direct portfolio drawdown is **$0.00 (0.0%)**; the de-risk trigger (one scenario plausibly hitting ≥3 positions hard) cannot fire against an empty book, and cash is already the maximum defensive state. No action required tonight.

Red-team summary:
- *Against reading the market-wide F&G "falling fast" flip as legitimate rather than a threshold artifact* — a skeptic could argue that 69→50 over a week is a normal cooldown from mild Greed, not the "falling fast from >70" blow-off-top pattern the rubric describes, and that the coded threshold (fg<60, Δ7d<−15) is over-broad, mechanically punishing every coin's ceiling by one on a reading that doesn't actually describe euphoria unwinding. Rebuttal: 69 sits one point under the rubric's own >70 line, and a −19-point weekly move is a genuinely fast decline by this book's own historical pattern (AM 09-16's milder −15 print was correctly read Neutral); treating this as a legitimate trigger rather than special-pleading it away for one point of proximity is the more disciplined read, and in any case it's moot this checkpoint — no coin was within 2 of the gate even before the flip.
- *Against reading p1 as Neutral across all 30 coins on a double data-source failure* — a skeptic could argue that going fully blind on sentiment for an entire checkpoint, especially for the 5 non-held coins sitting at the top of the mechanical board (BTC, UNI, ENA, ARB, ASTER), risks missing a live euphoria or capitulation extreme that would have flipped one of them Bearish or Bullish on p1 and mattered for the gate. Rebuttal: Section 0 is explicit that fabrication is worse than a Neutral default when both the API and web search genuinely fail to produce a dated read — none of these 5 coins were within 2 of the 7/10 gate on mechanical count alone, so even a maximally favorable p1 Bullish read would not have armed anyone this checkpoint; the miss-risk is real but bounded to zero trading consequence today, and is logged for the PM checkpoint to retry both fallbacks fresh.
- *Against holding all four positions unchanged with BNB's OI print sitting one point short of a Bearish trigger* — a skeptic could argue that −14.3% vs the −15% threshold is within rounding/noise distance and should be read as the "OI collapsing after a rally" pattern now rather than waiting for the number to cross a hard line. Rebuttal: the system's designed circuit breakers are the invalidation price and the 2-consecutive-checkpoint Bearish-count gate, not discretionary boundary-nudging on a single mechanical sub-metric; forcing this to Bearish without the threshold being met would be the same undisciplined pattern-forcing this book is built to avoid in the opposite (bullish) direction. Logged as a standing watch item, not an override.
